item.title: Dejima Dutch Trading Post — Guide
item.description: Dejima, a small fan-shaped artificial island in Nagasaki, was for more than two centuries Japan’s sole point of contact with the Western world. During the Edo period, when Japan closed itself to foreigners under the sakoku isolation policy, the Dutch East India Company was confined to this tiny island, making it the country’s only window onto Western trade, science and culture — knowledge that flowed into Japan as ‘Dutch learning’ (rangaku).

item.title: Huis Ten Bosch — Guide
item.description: Huis Ten Bosch, in Sasebo in western Nagasaki, is one of Japan’s largest theme parks, recreating a Dutch town in loving detail across a huge waterfront site. Named after a royal palace in the Netherlands, it features canals plied by boats, working windmills, brick townhouses, cobbled streets and grand European-style buildings, all set among vast seasonal flower gardens — a million tulips in spring, roses in early summer, and one of Japan’s most dazzling winter illuminations, with millions of lights.
